sal.basis: Swedes quote pay as gross monthly salary (månadslön), so per=month. Senior Financial Analyst / FP&A, ~8 yrs, Stockholm, base salary (bonus and holiday supplement excluded): about SEK 56,000 gross a month (about SEK 672k a year). Benchmarks recalled from Akavia (ex-Civilekonomerna) and SCB salary statistics and the Hays, Michael Page, Robert Walters and Poolia Sweden guides (2024-2026 editions), NOT re-verified this session (web search budget used up, page fetches failed): business controllers / financial analysts with 5-10 years in Stockholm about SEK 50-65k a month, senior FP&A analysts about SEK 52-62k, FP&A managers about SEK 65-85k. f = 56,000 / 26,000 = 2.154, so Noura's 34,000 SAR expectation maps to about SEK 73,200 a month, the FP&A-manager band. Gothenburg and Malmö pay roughly 5-10% less than Stockholm.

sensitive.notes: Swedish CVs sometimes carry a photo, but it is optional and Swedish CV guidance (including Arbetsförmedlingen's) says it is not needed, so we allow one but never ask for it. The Discrimination Act (2008:567) covers recruitment and protects sex, transgender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion or other belief, disability, sexual orientation and age, so we never ask gender, date of birth, nationality or marital status; these are outdated on Swedish CVs. Never put the personnummer on a CV: the Data Protection Act (2018:218) limits its use to clearly justified cases. Right to work is asked instead of nationality.

privacy.fr: Vos données sont protégées par le RGPD et la loi suédoise sur la protection des données, sous le contrôle de l'Autorité suédoise de protection de la vie privée (IMY).

culture.notes: Mon-Fri, about 40 hours (many agreements 38-40), with flexitime and hybrid work common. Hiring slows sharply from Midsummer to mid-August because most people take 3-4 weeks of summer holiday in July (25 days' statutory annual leave). Salaries are discussed as gross per month and paid monthly, usually on the 25th. Notice: the Employment Protection Act (LAS) sets at least 1 month for the employee, but white-collar collective agreements and senior contracts commonly give 2-3 months, so start dates for employed candidates are usually about 3 months out; a probationary period (provanställning) of up to 6 months is normal. CV: 1-2 pages, reverse chronological, photo optional, no personnummer. A short personal letter (personligt brev) is still common, though more employers now use screening questions instead. Ads often say 'urval sker löpande' (rolling selection), so applying early matters. References are checked at the final stage, and banks and listed companies often run background checks. Swedish is required at many domestic employers; Stockholm multinationals often work in English.
